products.name: The Woodshed
products.tagline: A living lead sheet that teaches you to reharmonize.
products.consumerDescription: An advanced interactive jazz practice suite: a Comping Coach that listens to your voicings, an Improv Heatmap that scores your lines, and a Concept Passport dashboard where you earn stamps in all 12 keys.

story.audience: Jazz pianists and comping players who know their tunes' changes but want to hear, and play, richer harmony.
story.problem: Reharmonization is usually learned from books and theory videos, away from the instrument. You read about substitutions but never feel them under your fingers, in time.
steps: Open a tune and The Woodshed lays it out as a living lead sheet.
Turn the reharmonization dial, or press a MIDI expression pedal, to add color from plain triads up to altered substitutions.
Plug in a MIDI keyboard: the Comping Coach listens to your voicings and the Improv Heatmap scores your lines.
Collect stamps in all 12 keys on your Concept Passport as each idea sticks.
features: Reharmonization dial with MIDI-pedal control
Comping Coach that listens to your voicings
Improv Heatmap that scores your lines
Concept Passport: track progress across all 12 keys
Runs in the browser, no install

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Engineered an interactive reharmonization engine connecting via MIDI expression pedals for dynamic chord complexity. Built a background Web Worker pipeline for traced generation and an "Engine X-ray" view, handling state transitions across a global circle-of-fifths memory.
engineeringSpecs.metrics: Live Practice Dashboard • MIDI Hardware Integrated

products.name: HeatReel
products.tagline: Skip to the parts everyone rewatches.
products.consumerDescription: A Chrome extension that auto-generates smart highlight reels on YouTube from the crowd's replay heatmap — with a custom mini-player overlay, keyboard shortcuts (Alt+S, Alt+X), and 1-click emoji-tiered timestamp comments.

story.audience: Anyone who watches long YouTube videos (podcasts, streams, lectures, matches) and wants the good part without scrubbing.
story.problem: YouTube already knows which moments everyone rewatches, but it only hints at it with a faint graph when you hover the progress bar.
steps: Install the extension and open any YouTube video that has a "most replayed" graph.
HeatReel reads the graph and finds the real peaks, not just the noise.
Watch the highlight reel in its mini-player, or drive it from the keyboard with Alt+S and Alt+X.
Drop a one-click, emoji-tiered timestamp comment on the moments that hit.
features: Auto-built highlight reel from the crowd's replay data
Custom mini-player overlay
Keyboard shortcuts (Alt+S, Alt+X)
One-click emoji timestamp comments
Runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Parses raw YouTube SVG heatmap path coordinates in real time, computing statistical intensity peaks (mean + standard deviation with a 15% fallback threshold) and syncing custom playback controls directly into the native video player lifecycle.
engineeringSpecs.metrics: Live on Chrome Web Store • Zero-backend client-side processing

products.name: PsychoScanner
products.tagline: Grade your psychometric practice test in seconds.
products.consumerDescription: A mobile OMR scanner that grades official Israeli Psychometric Entrance Exam (פסיכומטרי) answer sheets in seconds with your phone camera — supporting 19 official NITE practice exams (2020–2026) and instant 0–150 scaled scoring.

story.audience: Students preparing for the Israeli psychometric entrance exam (פסיכומטרי) who practice on official NITE exams at home.
story.problem: After a full practice test you still have to check every answer against the key by hand and work out the scaled score yourself. It's slow, error-prone, and the last thing you want after a three-hour exam.
steps: Choose which official practice exam you took (19 NITE exams, 2020–2026).
Photograph your bubble answer sheet. No scanner or flash needed.
The app finds the sheet, flattens it and reads every mark.
Get your results and a 0–150 scaled score in seconds.
features: Works with a phone camera on plain printouts
Copes with bent paper and dim lighting
19 official practice exams with answer keys built in
Instant scaled scoring
In beta on iOS & Android

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Custom OpenCV pipeline featuring anchor detection, perspective and paper-bend flattening, adaptive illumination normalization for dim no-flash B&W printouts, and lone-mark leniency — paired with an automated NITE PDF answer-key parser (parse_nite_pdfs.py).
engineeringSpecs.metrics: 19 Official Exams Indexed • Sub-second OMR Grading Pipeline

products.name: Bet on Dave
products.tagline: Ragdoll stunts. Your friends bet on how you fail.
products.consumerDescription: A chaotic physics-driven multiplayer "friendslop" game where players execute ragdoll stunts and spectators wager on the outcomes.

story.audience: Friend groups who love party games where failing is the funniest part.
story.problem: In most party games the people who aren't playing just wait for their turn. In Bet on Dave, watching is a game too.
steps: Players line up a ragdoll stunt.
Everyone watching bets on how it ends: clean landing, glorious wipeout, or something in between.
Physics decides, live and in sync for everyone in the lobby.
Bets pay out, and the stunt crew goes again.
features: Physics-driven ragdoll stunts
Live spectator betting
Online multiplayer with host-authoritative netcode
In development for PC

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Architected a host-authoritative state machine and core C# betting engine to synchronize physics-driven ragdoll mechanics and real-time spectator wagering over FishNet.
engineeringSpecs.metrics: Multiplayer Netcode Prototype • Edit-Mode Test Suites Passing

products.name: Idea5
products.tagline: Five minutes a day. One idea at a time.
products.consumerDescription: An offline-first phone app for a daily 5-minute idea ritual: a countdown that never interrupts you, a Markdown notepad, voice notes, streaks, searchable history and a daily calendar reminder. No account and no backend — everything stays on your device.

story.audience: People who want a small daily creative habit and keep bouncing off bloated note apps.
story.problem: Ideas get better with daily practice, but most note apps are built for storing things, not for showing up every day.
steps: Open Idea5 and start the 5-minute timer.
Write in Markdown or record a voice note. The timer never interrupts you.
Your streak grows and every session lands in a searchable history.
Add the daily reminder to your calendar so tomorrow's session is already booked.
features: Distraction-free 5-minute timer
Markdown notepad and voice notes
Streaks and searchable history
Works offline and installs like an app
No account: everything stays on your device, with zip backup & restore

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Drift-free timer modeled as accumulated time plus performance.now() deltas, so it survives throttled background tabs; debounced autosave with stale-draft recovery; voice clips stored as Blobs in Dexie with per-browser MIME detection; and zip backup/restore plus .ics reminder export — all on-device, with no server.
engineeringSpecs.metrics: Offline-first PWA • Zero backend • Unit-tested timer, streak & backup logic

products.name: Explorer2
products.tagline: File Explorer with tabs, split view and Total Commander keys.
products.consumerDescription: A Windows 11 File Explorer replacement with tabs, a side-by-side split view and Total Commander style keyboard control, built on the native Windows shell so context menus, thumbnails, drag & drop, previews and sharing all work exactly like File Explorer. Built together with my dad.

story.audience: Windows power users who move a lot of files around and miss the two-pane speed of Total Commander, without giving up the native Explorer they know.
story.problem: Windows File Explorer has no split view and little keyboard control, while classic two-pane file managers re-implement the shell and lose native context menus, previews and sharing.
steps: Download the standalone Explorer2.exe from the latest release and run it. It lives in the system tray.
Open tabs with Ctrl+T, or press Ctrl+Shift+S to split the window into two panes.
Mark files with Space, then copy with F5, move with F6 or peek inside with the F3 quick viewer.
Optionally make it your default, so folders and Win+E open in Explorer2.
features: Real Windows shell views in every tab
Split mode with Total Commander style function keys
F3 quick viewer for PDF, Office, images, text and hex
Preview pane, native Share sheet, light and dark mode
Tray app with optional Win+E replacement

engineeringSpecs.architectureHighlight: Hosts the native Windows shell view (IExplorerBrowser) inside each tab instead of re-implementing a file list, then layers a Total Commander style command system on top: marking, F5/F6 copy and move through Windows' own progress, conflict and undo handling, and registered preview handlers for the F3 quick viewer.
engineeringSpecs.metrics: v1.0.0 released • Co-built with my dad • MIT licensed
